- Don't wait forever between retries\n4. **Log retry attempts** - Use on_retry callback for observability\n5. **Only retry transient errors** - Use retry_if for selective retrying\n6. **Set timeouts for polling** - Use retry_until with timeout option\n"}, "Biblioteca padrão -> semver": {"id": "stdlib-semver", "content": "# @stdlib/semver - Semantic Versioning\n\nProvides parsing, comparison, and manipulation of semantic versions following the SemVer 2.0.0 specification.\n\n## Import\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse, compare, satisfies, increment } from \"@stdlib/semver\";\nimport { lt, gt, eq, lte, gte, neq } from \"@stdlib/semver\";\nimport { valid, major, minor, patch, sort } from \"@stdlib/semver\";\n```\n\n## Parsing and Formatting\n\n### parse(version: string): object\n\nParse a semantic version string.\n\n```hemlock\nlet v = parse(\"1.2.3-beta.1+build.456\");\nprint(v[\"major\"]); // 1\nprint(v[\"minor\"]); // 2\nprint(v[\"patch\"]); // 3\nprint(v[\"prerelease\"]); // \"beta.1\"\nprint(v[\"build\"]); // \"build.456\"\n\n// Leading 'v' is optional\nparse(\"v2.0.0\"); // Works\n```\n\n### format(ver: object): string\n\nConvert a version object back to string.\n\n```hemlock\nlet v = parse(\"1.2.3-alpha\");\nprint(format(v)); // \"1.2.3-alpha\"\n```\n\n## Comparison Functions\n\n### compare(a, b): i32\n\nCompare two versions. Returns -1, 0, or 1.\n\n```hemlock\ncompare(\"1.0.0\", \"2.0.0\"); // -1 (a < b)\ncompare(\"2.0.0\", \"1.0.0\"); // 1 (a > b)\ncompare(\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.0\"); // 0 (a == b)\n```\n\n### Comparison Operators\n\n```hemlock\nlt(\"1.0.0\", \"2.0.0\"); // true (less than)\nlte(\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.0\"); // true (less than or equal)\ngt(\"2.0.0\", \"1.0.0\"); // true (greater than)\ngte(\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.0\"); // true (greater than or equal)\neq(\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.0\"); // true (equal)\nneq(\"1.0.0\", \"2.0.0\"); // true (not equal)\n```\n\n### Prerelease Comparison\n\nFollows SemVer precedence rules:\n\n```hemlock\n// Release > prerelease\ncompare(\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.0-alpha\"); // 1\n\n// Alphabetic comparison\ncompare(\"1.0.0-alpha\", \"1.0.0-beta\"); // -1\n\n// Numeric identifiers compared as numbers\ncompare(\"1.0.0-alpha.1\", \"1.0.0-alpha.2\"); // -1\ncompare(\"1.0.0-alpha.10\", \"1.0.0-alpha.2\"); // 1\n\n// Longer prerelease > shorter\ncompare(\"1.0.0-alpha.1\", \"1.0.0-alpha.1.0\"); // -1\n```\n\n## Version Incrementing\n\n### increment(version, release, identifier?): string\n\nIncrement a version by release type.\n\n```hemlock\nincrement(\"1.2.3\", \"major\"); // \"2.0.0\"\nincrement(\"1.2.3\", \"minor\"); // \"1.3.0\"\nincrement(\"1.2.3\", \"patch\"); // \"1.2.4\"\n\n// Prerelease increments\nincrement(\"1.2.3\", \"prerelease\", \"alpha\"); // \"1.2.4-alpha\"\nincrement(\"1.2.4-alpha\", \"prerelease\"); // \"1.2.4-alpha.0\"\nincrement(\"1.2.4-alpha.0\", \"prerelease\"); // \"1.2.4-alpha.1\"\n\n// Pre-versions\nincrement(\"1.2.3\", \"premajor\", \"rc\"); // \"2.0.0-rc\"\nincrement(\"1.2.3\", \"preminor\", \"rc\"); // \"1.3.0-rc\"\nincrement(\"1.2.3\", \"prepatch\", \"rc\"); // \"1.2.4-rc\"\n```\n\n## Range Matching\n\n### satisfies(version, range): bool\n\nCheck if a version satisfies a range specification.\n\n```hemlock\n// Comparison operators\nsatisfies(\"1.2.3\", \">=1.0.0\"); // true\nsatisfies(\"1.2.3\", \"<2.0.0\"); // true\nsatisfies(\"1.2.3\", \"=1.2.3\"); // true\nsatisfies(\"1.2.3\", \"!=1.0.0\"); // true\n\n// Combined ranges (AND - space separated)\nsatisfies(\"1.2.3\", \">=1.0.0 <2.0.0\"); // true\n\n// OR ranges (|| separated)\nsatisfies(\"3.0.0\", \"^1.0.0 || ^3.0.0\"); // true\n```\n\n### Caret Ranges (^)\n\nAllows changes that don't modify the left-most non-zero digit.\n\n```hemlock\n// ^1.2.3 means >=1.2.3 <2.0.0\nsatisfies(\"1.5.0\", \"^1.2.3\"); // true\nsatisfies(\"2.0.0\", \"^1.2.3\"); // false\n\n// ^0.2.3 means >=0.2.3 <0.3.0\nsatisfies(\"0.2.5\", \"^0.2.3\"); // true\nsatisfies(\"0.3.0\", \"^0.2.3\"); // false\n\n// ^0.0.3 means >=0.0.3 <0.0.4\nsatisfies(\"0.0.3\", \"^0.0.3\"); // true\nsatisfies(\"0.0.4\", \"^0.0.3\"); // false\n```\n\n### Tilde Ranges (~)\n\nAllows patch-level changes.\n\n```hemlock\n// ~1.2.3 means >=1.2.3 <1.3.0\nsatisfies(\"1.2.5\", \"~1.2.3\"); // true\nsatisfies(\"1.3.0\", \"~1.2.3\"); // false\n```\n\n## Utility Functions\n\n### Version Part Extraction\n\n```hemlock\nmajor(\"1.2.3\"); // 1\nminor(\"1.2.3\"); // 2\npatch(\"1.2.3\"); // 3\nprerelease(\"1.0.0-alpha.1\"); // \"alpha.1\"\n```\n\n### Validation\n\n```hemlock\nvalid(\"1.2.3\"); // true\nvalid(\"1.2\"); // true (partial versions ok)\nvalid(\"invalid\"); // false\n```\n\n### Cleaning\n\n```hemlock\nclean(\"v1.2.3\"); // \"1.2.3\"\nclean(\"1.2.3-beta+build\"); // \"1.2.3-beta+build\"\n```\n\n### Min/Max\n\n```hemlock\nmax(\"1.0.0\", \"2.0.0\"); // \"2.0.0\"\nmin(\"1.0.0\", \"2.0.0\"); // \"1.0.0\"\n```\n\n### Sorting\n\n```hemlock\nlet versions = [\"2.0.0\", \"1.0.0\", \"1.5.0\", \"1.0.1\"];\n\nsort(versions); // [\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.1\", \"1.5.0\", \"2.0.0\"]\nrsort(versions); // [\"2.0.0\", \"1.5.0\", \"1.0.1\", \"1.0.0\"]\n```\n\n### Range Satisfaction\n\n```hemlock\nlet versions = [\"1.0.0\", \"1.2.0\", \"1.5.0\", \"2.0.0\"];\n\nmax_satisfying(versions, \"^1.0.0\"); // \"1.5.0\"\nmin_satisfying(versions, \"^1.0.0\"); // \"1.0.0\"\n```\n\n### Difference\n\n```hemlock\ndiff(\"1.0.0\", \"2.0.0\"); // \"major\"\ndiff(\"1.0.0\", \"1.1.0\"); // \"minor\"\ndiff(\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.1\"); // \"patch\"\ndiff(\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.0-alpha\"); // \"prerelease\"\ndiff(\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.0\"); // null\n```\n\n## Examples\n\n### Dependency Version Checking\n\n```hemlock\nimport { satisfies, max_satisfying } from \"@stdlib/semver\";\n\nlet required = \"^2.0.0\";\nlet available = [\"1.5.0\", \"2.0.0\", \"2.1.0\", \"2.5.0\", \"3.0.0\"];\n\nlet best = max_satisfying(available, required);\nif (best != null) {\n print(\"Using version: \" + best); // \"2.5.0\"\n} else {\n print(\"No compatible version found\");\n}\n```\n\n### Version Bumping Script\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse, increment, format } from \"@stdlib/semver\";\n\nfn bump_version(current: string, change_type: string): string {\n return increment(current, change_type);\n}\n\nlet version = \"1.2.3\";\nprint(\"Current: \" + version);\nprint(\"After patch: \" + bump_version(version, \"patch\"));\nprint(\"After minor: \" + bump_version(version, \"minor\"));\nprint(\"After major: \" + bump_version(version, \"major\"));\n```\n\n### Sorting Releases\n\n```hemlock\nimport { rsort } from \"@stdlib/semver\";\n\nlet releases = [\n \"1.0.0\",\n \"1.0.0-alpha\",\n \"1.0.0-beta\",\n \"1.0.0-rc.1\",\n \"1.0.0-rc.2\",\n \"0.9.0\"\n];\n\nlet sorted = rsort(releases);\nprint(\"Latest: \" + sorted[0]); // \"1.0.0\"\n```\n\n## SemVer Specification\n\nThis module follows the Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification:\n\n- Format: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]`\n- MAJOR: Incremented for incompatible API changes\n- MINOR: Incremented for backwards-compatible features\n- PATCH: Incremented for backwards-compatible bug fixes\n- PRERELEASE: Optional, indicates unstable version\n- BUILD: Optional metadata, ignored in comparisons\n\nSee: https://semver.org/\n"}, "Biblioteca padrão -> shell": {"id": "stdlib-shell", "content": "# @stdlib/shell - Shell Utilities\n\nProvides utilities for building shell commands safely, escaping arguments, parsing output, and executing commands.\n\n## Import\n\n```hemlock\nimport { escape, quote, run, run_capture } from \"@stdlib/shell\";\nimport { which, command_exists, env_or } from \"@stdlib/shell\";\nimport { build_command, pipe, and_then } from \"@stdlib/shell\";\n```\n\n## Argument Escaping\n\n### escape(s: string): string\n\nEscape shell metacharacters with backslashes.\n\n```hemlock\nescape(\"hello world\"); // \"hello\\ world\"\nescape(\"$HOME\"); // \"\\$HOME\"\nescape(\"test*.txt\"); // \"test\\*.txt\"\nescape(\"a & b; c\"); // \"a\\ \\&\\ b\\;\\ c\"\n```\n\n### quote(s: string): string\n\nQuote a string with single quotes (safest method).\n\n```hemlock\nquote(\"hello world\"); // \"'hello world'\"\nquote(\"it's fine\"); // \"'it'\\\"'\\\"'s fine'\"\nquote(\"$HOME\"); // \"'$HOME'\" (no expansion)\n```\n\n### double_quote(s: string): string\n\nQuote with double quotes (allows variable expansion in shell).\n\n```hemlock\ndouble_quote(\"$HOME\"); // \"\\\"\\\\$HOME\\\"\"\ndouble_quote('say \"hi\"'); // \"\\\"say \\\\\\\"hi\\\\\\\"\\\"\"\n```\n\n## Command Building\n\n### build_command(parts: array): string\n\nBuild a command string from parts, quoting each argument.\n\n```hemlock\nbuild_command([\"ls\", \"-la\", \"/tmp\"]);\n// \"'ls' '-la' '/tmp'\"\n\nbuild_command([\"grep\", \"hello world\", \"file.txt\"]);\n// \"'grep' 'hello world' 'file.txt'\"\n```\n\n### Command Chaining\n\n```hemlock\n// Run second only if first succeeds\nand_then([\"cmd1\", \"cmd2\"]); // \"cmd1 && cmd2\"\n\n// Run second only if first fails\nor_else([\"cmd1\", \"cmd2\"]); // \"cmd1 || cmd2\"\n\n// Run all regardless of success\nsequential([\"cmd1\", \"cmd2\", \"cmd3\"]); // \"cmd1; cmd2; cmd3\"\n\n// Pipe output\npipe([\"cat file\", \"grep pattern\", \"wc -l\"]);\n// \"cat file | grep pattern | wc -l\"\n```\n\n## Command Execution\n\n### run(command): bool\n\nRun a command and return success status.\n\n```hemlock\nif (run(\"make build\")) {\n print(\"Build succeeded!\");\n}\n\n// With array (auto-quoted)\nrun([\"cp\", \"source file.txt\", \"dest/\"]);\n```\n\n### run_capture(command): object\n\nRun and capture output.\n\n```hemlock\nlet result = run_capture(\"git status\");\nif (result[\"success\"]) {\n print(result[\"stdout\"]);\n} else {\n print(\"Error: \" + result[\"stderr\"]);\n}\n\n// Result object:\n// {\n// success: bool,\n// stdout: string,\n// stderr: string,\n// code: i32\n// }\n```\n\n### run_output(command): string\n\nRun and return stdout, throw on failure.\n\n```hemlock\nlet version = run_output(\"python --version\");\nprint(version); // \"Python 3.9.7\"\n```\n\n### run_lines(command): array\n\nRun and return stdout as array of lines.\n\n```hemlock\nlet files = run_lines(\"ls -1 /tmp\");\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < files.length) {\n print(\"File: \" + files[i]);\n i = i + 1;\n}\n```\n\n## Environment\n\n### env_or(name, default): string\n\nGet environment variable or default value.\n\n```hemlock\nlet home = env_or(\"HOME\", \"/tmp\");\nlet editor = env_or(\"EDITOR\", \"nano\");\n```\n\n### has_env(name): bool\n\nCheck if environment variable is set and non-empty.\n\n```hemlock\nif (has_env(\"DEBUG\")) {\n print(\"Debug mode enabled\");\n}\n```\n\n### set_envs(vars: object)\n\nSet multiple environment variables.\n\n```hemlock\nset_envs({\n PATH: \"/usr/bin:/bin\",\n HOME: \"/home/user\"\n});\n```\n\n## Path Utilities\n\n### which(command): string or null\n\nFind command path, or null if not found.\n\n```hemlock\nlet python = which(\"python3\");\nif (python != null) {\n print(\"Python at: \" + python);\n}\n```\n\n### command_exists(command): bool\n\nCheck if command exists in PATH.\n\n```hemlock\nif (command_exists(\"docker\")) {\n print(\"Docker is available\");\n}\n```\n\n## File Operations\n\n```hemlock\nfile_exists(\"/etc/passwd\"); // true\ndir_exists(\"/tmp\"); // true\n\nmkdir(\"/path/to/dir\"); // Create directory (with parents)\nrm(\"/tmp/file.txt\"); // Remove file\nrm(\"/tmp/dir\", true); // Remove directory recursively\n\ncp(\"src.txt\", \"dst.txt\"); // Copy file\ncp(\"/src/dir\", \"/dst/dir\", true); // Copy directory recursively\n\nmv(\"old.txt\", \"new.txt\"); // Move/rename\n```\n\n## Output Parsing\n\n### parse_columns(line): array\n\nParse whitespace-separated columns.\n\n```hemlock\nlet cols = parse_columns(\" col1 col2 col3 \");\n// [\"col1\", \"col2\", \"col3\"]\n```\n\n### parse_env_output(output): object\n\nParse KEY=VALUE output.\n\n```hemlock\nlet env = parse_env_output(\"FOO=bar\\nBAZ=qux\");\nprint(env[\"FOO\"]); // \"bar\"\nprint(env[\"BAZ\"]); // \"qux\"\n```\n\n### parse_table(output): array\n\nParse tabular output with header row.\n\n```hemlock\nlet output = \"NAME SIZE DATE\\nfile1 100 2024-01-01\\nfile2 200 2024-01-02\";\nlet rows = parse_table(output);\n// [\n// { NAME: \"file1\", SIZE: \"100\", DATE: \"2024-01-01\" },\n// { NAME: \"file2\", SIZE: \"200\", DATE: \"2024-01-02\" }\n// ]\n```\n\n## Redirection\n\n```hemlock\nredirect_stdout(\"cmd\", \"out.txt\"); // \"cmd > 'out.txt'\"\nredirect_stderr(\"cmd\", \"err.txt\"); // \"cmd 2> 'err.txt'\"\nredirect_all(\"cmd\", \"log.txt\"); // \"cmd > 'log.txt' 2>&1\"\n```\n\n## Background Execution\n\n```hemlock\nbackground(\"long_task\"); // \"long_task &\"\nsubshell(\"cd /tmp && ls\"); // \"(cd /tmp && ls)\"\nnohup(\"daemon\", \"/var/log/out.log\"); // \"nohup daemon > '/var/log/out.log' 2>&1 &\"\n```\n\n## Examples\n\n### Safe Command Execution\n\n```hemlock\nimport { build_command, run, run_output } from \"@stdlib/shell\";\n\nfn backup_file(source: string, dest: string): bool {\n let cmd = build_command([\"cp\", \"-p\", source, dest]);\n return run(cmd);\n}\n\n// Safe even with spaces or special characters\nbackup_file(\"/path/to/my file.txt\", \"/backup/my file.txt\");\n```\n\n### Script Automation\n\n```hemlock\nimport { run, run_capture, command_exists, and_then } from \"@stdlib/shell\";\n\nfn deploy() {\n // Check prerequisites\n if (!command_exists(\"docker\")) {\n throw \"Docker not installed\";\n }\n if (!command_exists(\"kubectl\")) {\n throw \"kubectl not installed\";\n }\n\n // Build and push\n let result = run_capture(and_then([\n \"docker build -t myapp:latest .\",\n \"docker push myapp:latest\",\n \"kubectl apply -f k8s/\"\n ]));\n\n if (!result[\"success\"]) {\n print(\"Deploy failed: \" + result[\"stderr\"]);\n return false;\n }\n\n return true;\n}\n```\n\n### Parsing Command Output\n\n```hemlock\nimport { run_lines, parse_columns } from \"@stdlib/shell\";\n\nfn list_processes() {\n let lines = run_lines(\"ps aux\");\n let i = 1; // Skip header\n while (i < lines.length) {\n let cols = parse_columns(lines[i]);\n if (cols.length >= 11) {\n print(\"PID: \" + cols[1] + \", CMD: \" + cols[10]);\n }\n i = i + 1;\n }\n}\n```\n\n### Environment Setup\n\n```hemlock\nimport { env_or, set_envs, has_env } from \"@stdlib/shell\";\n\nfn setup_environment() {\n // Get with defaults\n let node_env = env_or(\"NODE_ENV\", \"development\");\n let port = env_or(\"PORT\", \"3000\");\n\n // Set multiple\n set_envs({\n APP_ENV: node_env,\n APP_PORT: port,\n APP_DEBUG: has_env(\"DEBUG\") ? \"1\" : \"0\"\n });\n}\n```\n\n## Safe Execution (No Shell Injection)\n\nThe `*_safe` functions use `exec_argv` internally, which bypasses shell interpretation entirely. This prevents shell injection attacks and properly captures both stdout and stderr separately.\n\n### exec_safe(argv: array): object\n\nExecute command without shell interpretation. Returns full result object.\n\n```hemlock\nlet result = exec_safe([\"ls\", \"-la\", \"/tmp\"]);\nprint(result.output); // stdout\nprint(result.stderr); // stderr (properly captured!)\nprint(result.exit_code); // 0 on success\n```\n\n### run_capture_safe(argv: array): object\n\nRun command safely and return structured result with proper stderr capture.\n\n```hemlock\nlet result = run_capture_safe([\"git\", \"commit\", \"-m\", \"message\"]);\n// Returns: { success: bool, stdout: string, stderr: string, code: i32 }\n\nif (!result.success) {\n print(\"Git error: \" + result.stderr);\n}\n```\n\n### run_output_safe(argv: array): string\n\nRun command safely and return stdout, or throw on failure.\n\n```hemlock\nlet version = run_output_safe([\"python3\", \"--version\"]);\nprint(version); // \"Python 3.9.7\\n\"\n```\n\n### run_safe(argv: array): bool\n\nRun command safely and return success status.\n\n```hemlock\nif (run_safe([\"make\", \"build\"])) {\n print(\"Build succeeded!\");\n}\n```\n\n### Shell Injection Protection\n\n```hemlock\n// DANGEROUS: shell interprets the semicolon\nrun(\"echo \" + user_input); // user_input = \"hello; rm -rf /\"\n\n// SAFE: no shell interpretation, semicolon is literal\nrun_safe([\"echo\", user_input]); // Outputs: \"hello; rm -rf /\"\n```\n\n### When to Use Safe vs Regular Functions\n\n| Use Case | Function | Reason |\n|----------|----------|--------|\n| User-provided arguments | `*_safe` functions | Prevents injection |\n| Need stderr separate | `exec_safe`, `run_capture_safe` | Proper pipe separation |\n| Shell features needed | `run`, `run_capture` | Pipes, redirects, globs |\n| Simple commands | Either | Both work fine |\n\n## Security Notes\n\n- Always use `quote()` or `build_command()` for user input with shell functions\n- **Prefer `*_safe` functions** (`exec_safe`, `run_safe`, etc.) for untrusted input\n- Use `run([\"cmd\", arg1, arg2])` over string concatenation when using shell functions\n- Validate paths before file operations\n- Be cautious with `rm(..., true)` (recursive delete)\n"}, "Biblioteca padrão -> signal": {"id": "stdlib-signal", "content": "# Signal Constants Module (`@stdlib/signal`)\n\nA standard library module providing signal handling functions and POSIX signal constants.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe signal module provides named constants for POSIX signals, organized into four categories:\n\n- **Terminal signals** - Process termination and interruption (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT, SIGABRT)\n- **User-defined signals** - Application-specific signaling (SIGUSR1, SIGUSR2)\n- **Miscellaneous signals** - Timers, child processes, pipes (SIGALRM, SIGCHLD, SIGPIPE)\n- **Job control signals** - Process stop/continue and terminal I/O (SIGCONT, SIGSTOP, SIGTSTP, SIGTTIN, SIGTTOU)\n\n## Usage\n\n```hemlock\nimport { signal, raise, SIGINT, SIGTERM } from \"@stdlib/signal\";\n\nsignal(SIGINT, fn(sig) {\n print(\"Caught interrupt signal\");\n});\n```\n\nOr import all:\n\n```hemlock\nimport * as sig from \"@stdlib/signal\";\n\nsig.signal(sig.SIGINT, fn(s) {\n print(\"Interrupted\");\n});\n```\n\n---\n\n## Signal Functions\n\nAs of v2.0.0, the `signal()` and `raise()` functions are exported from this module.\n\n### signal(signum, handler)\n\nRegister a signal handler function.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `signum: i32` - Signal number (use constants like `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`)\n- `handler: function | null` - Function to call when signal is received, or `null` to reset to default\n\nThe handler may be declared with **one parameter** to receive the signal\nnumber (`fn(sig) { ... }`) or with **no parameters** if it does not need it\n(`fn() { ... }`). Both forms are valid; a zero-parameter handler simply does\nnot receive the signal number.\n\n**Returns:** The previous handler function (or `null` if none was registered)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { signal, SIGINT } from \"@stdlib/signal\";\n\nfn my_handler(sig) {\n print(\"Caught signal: \" + typeof(sig));\n}\n\nlet old = signal(SIGINT, my_handler);\n\n// Reset to default behavior\nsignal(SIGINT, null);\n```\n\n### raise(signum)\n\nSend a signal to the current process.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `signum: i32` - Signal number to send\n\n**Returns:** `null`\n\n```hemlock\nimport { signal, raise, SIGUSR1 } from \"@stdlib/signal\";\n\nlet count = 0;\n\nsignal(SIGUSR1, fn(sig) {\n count = count + 1;\n});\n\nraise(SIGUSR1);\nprint(count); // 1\n```\n\n---\n\n## Terminal Signals\n\n### SIGINT\nInterrupt signal, sent when the user presses **Ctrl+C**. Commonly used to implement graceful shutdown.\n\n**Default behavior:** Terminate the process.\n\n### SIGTERM\nTermination request signal. Sent by `kill` command by default. The standard way to politely ask a process to exit.\n\n**Default behavior:** Terminate the process.\n\n### SIGHUP\nHangup signal, originally sent when a terminal connection was lost. Often used to request configuration reload in daemons.\n\n**Default behavior:** Terminate the process.\n\n### SIGQUIT\nQuit signal, sent when the user presses **Ctrl+\\\\**. Similar to SIGINT but typically produces a core dump.\n\n**Default behavior:** Terminate the process (with core dump).\n\n### SIGABRT\nAbort signal. Sent by the `abort()` C function or by `panic()` in Hemlock. Indicates an abnormal termination.\n\n**Default behavior:** Terminate the process (with core dump).\n\n---\n\n## User-Defined Signals\n\n### SIGUSR1\nUser-defined signal 1. Has no predefined meaning - available for application-specific purposes.\n\n**Default behavior:** Terminate the process.\n\n### SIGUSR2\nUser-defined signal 2. Has no predefined meaning - available for application-specific purposes.\n\n**Default behavior:** Terminate the process.\n\n---\n\n## Miscellaneous Signals\n\n### SIGALRM\nAlarm signal, sent when a timer set by `alarm()` expires. Useful for implementing timeouts.\n\n**Default behavior:** Terminate the process.\n\n### SIGCHLD\nChild process status changed. Sent to the parent when a child process stops or terminates.\n\n**Default behavior:** Ignored.\n\n### SIGPIPE\nBroken pipe. Sent when writing to a pipe or socket whose reading end has been closed.\n\n**Default behavior:** Terminate the process.\n\n---\n\n## Job Control Signals\n\n### SIGCONT\nContinue signal. Resumes a process that was stopped by SIGSTOP or SIGTSTP.\n\n**Default behavior:** Continue the process if stopped; otherwise ignored.\n\n### SIGSTOP\nStop signal. Suspends the process. **Cannot be caught or ignored** - the handler will not be called.\n\n**Default behavior:** Stop the process (unconditional).\n\n### SIGTSTP\nTerminal stop signal, sent when the user presses **Ctrl+Z**. Unlike SIGSTOP, this signal can be caught.\n\n**Default behavior:** Stop the process.\n\n### SIGTTIN\nBackground read signal. Sent to a background process that attempts to read from the terminal.\n\n**Default behavior:** Stop the process.\n\n### SIGTTOU\nBackground write signal. Sent to a background process that attempts to write to the terminal.\n\n**Default behavior:** Stop the process.\n\n---\n\n## Constants Reference\n\n| Constant | Description | Catchable |\n|----------|-------------|-----------|\n| `SIGINT` | Interrupt (Ctrl+C) | Yes |\n| `SIGTERM` | Termination request | Yes |\n| `SIGHUP` | Hangup (terminal closed) | Yes |\n| `SIGQUIT` | Quit (Ctrl+\\\\) | Yes |\n| `SIGABRT` | Abort | Yes |\n| `SIGUSR1` | User-defined signal 1 | Yes |\n| `SIGUSR2` | User-defined signal 2 | Yes |\n| `SIGALRM` | Alarm timer expired | Yes |\n| `SIGCHLD` | Child process status changed | Yes |\n| `SIGPIPE` | Broken pipe | Yes |\n| `SIGCONT` | Continue if stopped | Yes |\n| `SIGSTOP` | Stop process | **No** |\n| `SIGTSTP` | Terminal stop (Ctrl+Z) | Yes |\n| `SIGTTIN` | Background read from terminal | Yes |\n| `SIGTTOU` | Background write to terminal | Yes |\n\n---\n\n## Examples\n\n### Graceful Shutdown on Ctrl+C\n\n```hemlock\nimport { signal, SIGINT, SIGTERM } from \"@stdlib/signal\";\n\nlet running = true;\n\nfn shutdown(sig) {\n print(\"Shutting down gracefully...\");\n running = false;\n}\n\nsignal(SIGINT, shutdown);\nsignal(SIGTERM, shutdown);\n\nwhile (running) {\n // ... do work ...\n}\n\nprint(\"Cleanup complete\");\n```\n\n### Configuration Reload with SIGHUP\n\n```hemlock\nimport { signal, SIGHUP } from \"@stdlib/signal\";\n\nlet config = { timeout: 30, debug: false };\n\nfn reload_config(sig) {\n print(\"Reloading configuration...\");\n // Re-read config file\n config = { timeout: 60, debug: true };\n print(\"Configuration reloaded\");\n}\n\nsignal(SIGHUP, reload_config);\n\n// Main loop - send SIGHUP to reload without restarting\nwhile (true) {\n // ... serve requests using config ...\n}\n```\n\n### Inter-Process Communication with SIGUSR1\n\n```hemlock\nimport { signal, SIGUSR1 } from \"@stdlib/signal\";\nimport { get_pid } from \"@stdlib/env\";\n\nlet event_count = 0;\n\nsignal(SIGUSR1, fn(sig) {\n event_count = event_count + 1;\n print(\"Event received! Total: \" + event_count);\n});\n\nprint(\"PID: \" + get_pid());\nprint(\"Send SIGUSR1 to trigger events\");\n\n// Keep running, waiting for signals\nwhile (true) {\n // ... do work ...\n}\n```\n\n### Raising Signals\n\n```hemlock\nimport { signal, raise, SIGUSR1, SIGUSR2 } from \"@stdlib/signal\";\n\nlet state = \"idle\";\n\nsignal(SIGUSR1, fn(sig) {\n state = \"processing\";\n print(\"State changed to: \" + state);\n});\n\nsignal(SIGUSR2, fn(sig) {\n state = \"idle\";\n print(\"State changed to: \" + state);\n});\n\n// Send a signal to the current process\nraise(SIGUSR1); // Triggers the SIGUSR1 handler\nprint(\"Current state: \" + state);\n\nraise(SIGUSR2); // Triggers the SIGUSR2 handler\nprint(\"Current state: \" + state);\n```\n\n### Ignoring SIGPIPE for Network Servers\n\n```hemlock\nimport { signal, SIGPIPE } from \"@stdlib/signal\";\n\n// Ignore broken pipe errors (common in network servers)\nsignal(SIGPIPE, fn(sig) {\n // Intentionally empty - ignore the signal\n});\n\n// Now writing to closed sockets won't crash the server\n// ... server code ...\n```\n\n### Timeout with SIGALRM\n\n```hemlock\nimport { signal, raise, SIGALRM } from \"@stdlib/signal\";\n\nlet timed_out = false;\n\nsignal(SIGALRM, fn(sig) {\n timed_out = true;\n print(\"Operation timed out!\");\n});\n\n// Set an alarm for 5 seconds\nraise(SIGALRM); // For demonstration; in practice, use alarm() via FFI\n\nif (timed_out) {\n print(\"Handling timeout...\");\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Notes\n\n- As of v2.0.0, `signal()` and `raise()` must be imported from `@stdlib/signal` along with the signal constants. Previously, they were available as global builtins.\n- Signal constants are integer values matching POSIX definitions on the host platform.\n- SIGSTOP cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored. Registering a handler for SIGSTOP has no effect.\n- Signal handlers should be kept short and simple. Avoid allocating memory or performing complex operations inside handlers.\n- Signal handling interacts with async tasks - signals are delivered to the main thread.\n- Added in v2.0.0. Previously, signal constants were available as global constants without importing.\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- **Environment module** (`@stdlib/env`) - Process control with `exit()` and `get_pid()`\n- **Process module** (`@stdlib/process`) - Fork, exec, wait, kill\n- **Async** - Structured concurrency with spawn/join\n\n---\n\n## License\n\nPart of the Hemlock standard library.\n"}, "Biblioteca padrão -> sqlite": {"id": "stdlib-sqlite", "content": "# Hemlock SQLite Module\n\nA standard library module providing SQLite3 database operations for Hemlock programs via FFI.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe sqlite module provides comprehensive SQLite3 database functionality:\n\n- **Connection management** - Open, close, and manage database connections\n- **Query execution** - Execute SQL with parameter binding\n- **Result handling** - Fetch results as arrays of objects\n- **Transactions** - Begin, commit, rollback with automatic handling\n- **Prepared statements** - Efficient repeated query execution\n- **Schema utilities** - Table existence checks, listing, column info\n\n## Usage\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, query, exec, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"mydata.db\");\n\n// Create a table\nexec(db, \"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, age INTEGER)\");\n\n// Insert data with parameters\nexec(db, \"INSERT INTO users (name, age) VALUES (?, ?)\", [\"Alice\", 30]);\nexec(db, \"INSERT INTO users (name, age) VALUES (?, ?)\", [\"Bob\", 25]);\n\n// Query data\nlet users = query(db, \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE age > ?\", [20]);\nfor (user in users) {\n print(user.name + \" is \" + typeof(user.age) + \" years old\");\n}\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\nOr import all:\n\n```hemlock\nimport * as sqlite from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = sqlite.open_db(\":memory:\");\n// ...\nsqlite.close_db(db);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Database Connection\n\n### open_db(path)\n\nOpens a database connection.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `path: string` - Path to database file, or `:memory:` for in-memory database\n\n**Returns:** `Database` - Database connection object\n\n**Throws:** Exception if database cannot be opened\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\n// Open a file-based database\nlet db = open_db(\"myapp.db\");\n\n// Open an in-memory database\nlet mem_db = open_db(\":memory:\");\n\n// Always close when done\nclose_db(db);\nclose_db(mem_db);\n```\n\n### open_db_flags(path, flags)\n\nOpens a database with specific flags.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `path: string` - Path to database file\n- `flags: i32` - Combination of open flags\n\n**Returns:** `Database` - Database connection object\n\n**Available flags:**\n- `SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY` - Open for reading only\n- `SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE` - Open for reading and writing\n- `SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE` - Create if doesn't exist (use with READWRITE)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db_flags, SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\n// Open read-only\nlet db = open_db_flags(\"data.db\", SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY);\n```\n\n### close_db(db)\n\nCloses a database connection.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection to close\n\n**Returns:** `null`\n\n**Throws:** Exception if close fails\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"test.db\");\n// ... use database ...\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### memory_db()\n\nCreates an in-memory database (convenience function).\n\n**Returns:** `Database` - In-memory database connection\n\n```hemlock\nimport { memory_db, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = memory_db();\n// Database exists only in memory\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Query Execution\n\n### exec(db, sql, params?)\n\nExecutes a SQL statement without returning results.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `sql: string` - SQL statement (use `?` for parameters)\n- `params: array` (optional) - Parameter values\n\n**Returns:** `null`\n\n**Throws:** Exception on SQL error\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, exec, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\":memory:\");\n\n// Create table\nexec(db, \"CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, price REAL)\");\n\n// Insert with parameters (prevents SQL injection)\nexec(db, \"INSERT INTO products (name, price) VALUES (?, ?)\", [\"Widget\", 9.99]);\nexec(db, \"INSERT INTO products (name, price) VALUES (?, ?)\", [\"Gadget\", 19.99]);\n\n// Update\nexec(db, \"UPDATE products SET price = ? WHERE name = ?\", [24.99, \"Gadget\"]);\n\n// Delete\nexec(db, \"DELETE FROM products WHERE price < ?\", [10.0]);\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### query(db, sql, params?)\n\nExecutes a query and returns all results.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `sql: string` - SQL SELECT statement\n- `params: array` (optional) - Parameter values\n\n**Returns:** `array` - Array of row objects\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, query, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"store.db\");\n\n// Get all products\nlet products = query(db, \"SELECT * FROM products\");\nfor (p in products) {\n print(p.name + \": $\" + typeof(p.price));\n}\n\n// Query with parameters\nlet expensive = query(db, \"SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > ?\", [50.0]);\n\n// Query with multiple parameters\nlet filtered = query(db,\n \"SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN ? AND ? ORDER BY name\",\n [10.0, 100.0]\n);\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### query_one(db, sql, params?)\n\nExecutes a query and returns only the first row.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `sql: string` - SQL SELECT statement\n- `params: array` (optional) - Parameter values\n\n**Returns:** Row object or `null` if no results\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, query_one, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"users.db\");\n\nlet user = query_one(db, \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?\", [42]);\nif (user != null) {\n print(\"Found: \" + user.name);\n} else {\n print(\"User not found\");\n}\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### query_value(db, sql, params?)\n\nExecutes a query and returns a single value (first column of first row).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `sql: string` - SQL SELECT statement\n- `params: array` (optional) - Parameter values\n\n**Returns:** Single value or `null`\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, query_value, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"store.db\");\n\n// Get a count\nlet total = query_value(db, \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products\");\nprint(\"Total products: \" + typeof(total));\n\n// Get max price\nlet max_price = query_value(db, \"SELECT MAX(price) FROM products\");\n\n// Get specific value\nlet name = query_value(db, \"SELECT name FROM products WHERE id = ?\", [1]);\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Convenience Functions\n\n### insert(db, sql, params?)\n\nInserts a row and returns the last insert rowid.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `sql: string` - INSERT statement\n- `params: array` (optional) - Parameter values\n\n**Returns:** `i64` - Last insert rowid\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, insert, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"users.db\");\n\nlet id = insert(db, \"INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n [\"Alice\", \"alice@example.com\"]);\nprint(\"Inserted user with ID: \" + typeof(id));\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### update(db, sql, params?)\n\nUpdates rows and returns the number of changes.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `sql: string` - UPDATE statement\n- `params: array` (optional) - Parameter values\n\n**Returns:** `i32` - Number of rows affected\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, update, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"products.db\");\n\nlet changed = update(db, \"UPDATE products SET price = price * 1.1 WHERE category = ?\",\n [\"electronics\"]);\nprint(\"Updated \" + typeof(changed) + \" products\");\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### delete_rows(db, sql, params?)\n\nDeletes rows and returns the number of changes.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `sql: string` - DELETE statement\n- `params: array` (optional) - Parameter values\n\n**Returns:** `i32` - Number of rows deleted\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, delete_rows, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"logs.db\");\n\nlet deleted = delete_rows(db, \"DELETE FROM logs WHERE created_at < ?\",\n [\"2024-01-01\"]);\nprint(\"Deleted \" + typeof(deleted) + \" old logs\");\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### count(db, table_name, where_clause?)\n\nCounts rows in a table.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `table_name: string` - Name of the table\n- `where_clause: string` (optional) - WHERE clause without \"WHERE\"\n\n**Returns:** `i64` - Number of rows\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, count, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"store.db\");\n\nlet total = count(db, \"products\");\nprint(\"Total products: \" + typeof(total));\n\nlet active = count(db, \"products\", \"active = 1\");\nprint(\"Active products: \" + typeof(active));\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Transactions\n\n### begin(db)\n\nBegins a transaction (DEFERRED).\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, begin, commit, rollback, exec, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"bank.db\");\n\nbegin(db);\ntry {\n exec(db, \"UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = ?\", [1]);\n exec(db, \"UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = ?\", [2]);\n commit(db);\n} catch (e) {\n rollback(db);\n print(\"Transaction failed: \" + e);\n}\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### begin_immediate(db)\n\nBegins an immediate transaction (acquires write lock immediately).\n\n### begin_exclusive(db)\n\nBegins an exclusive transaction (acquires exclusive lock).\n\n### commit(db)\n\nCommits the current transaction.\n\n### rollback(db)\n\nRolls back the current transaction.\n\n### transaction(db, callback)\n\nExecutes a function within a transaction with automatic commit/rollback.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `callback: fn` - Function to execute\n\n**Returns:** Return value of callback\n\n**Throws:** Re-throws callback exceptions after rollback\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, transaction, exec, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"bank.db\");\n\n// Automatic transaction handling\nlet result = transaction(db, fn() {\n exec(db, \"UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1\");\n exec(db, \"UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 2\");\n return \"Transfer complete\";\n});\n\nprint(result); // \"Transfer complete\"\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Prepared Statements\n\nFor repeated queries, prepared statements are more efficient.\n\n### prepare(db, sql)\n\nPrepares a SQL statement.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `sql: string` - SQL statement\n\n**Returns:** `Statement` - Prepared statement object\n\n### stmt_bind(stmt, params)\n\nBinds parameters to a prepared statement. Resets the statement and clears previous bindings before applying new ones.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `stmt: Statement` - Prepared statement object\n- `params: array` - Parameter values to bind\n\n**Returns:** `null`\n\n**Throws:** Exception if statement is finalized or binding fails\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, prepare, stmt_bind, stmt_exec, stmt_finalize, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\":memory:\");\nexec(db, \"CREATE TABLE items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)\");\n\nlet stmt = prepare(db, \"INSERT INTO items (name) VALUES (?)\");\n\n// Bind and execute separately\nstmt_bind(stmt, [\"Widget\"]);\nstmt_exec(stmt);\n\nstmt_finalize(stmt);\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### stmt_exec(stmt, params?)\n\nExecutes a prepared statement (for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE).\n\n### stmt_query(stmt, params?)\n\nExecutes a prepared statement and returns results (for SELECT).\n\n### stmt_finalize(stmt)\n\nFinalizes a prepared statement (releases resources).\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, prepare, stmt_exec, stmt_query, stmt_finalize, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\":memory:\");\nexec(db, \"CREATE TABLE items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)\");\n\n// Prepare insert statement\nlet insert_stmt = prepare(db, \"INSERT INTO items (name) VALUES (?)\");\n\n// Execute multiple times efficiently\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < 1000) {\n stmt_exec(insert_stmt, [\"Item \" + typeof(i)]);\n i = i + 1;\n}\nstmt_finalize(insert_stmt);\n\n// Prepare select statement\nlet select_stmt = prepare(db, \"SELECT * FROM items WHERE id > ?\");\n\nlet items = stmt_query(select_stmt, [990]);\nprint(\"Found \" + typeof(items.length) + \" items\");\n\nstmt_finalize(select_stmt);\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Schema Utilities\n\n### table_exists(db, table_name)\n\nChecks if a table exists.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `db: Database` - Database connection\n- `table_name: string` - Name of the table\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - True if table exists\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, table_exists, exec, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"app.db\");\n\nif (!table_exists(db, \"users\")) {\n exec(db, \"CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)\");\n}\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### list_tables(db)\n\nLists all tables in the database.\n\n**Returns:** `array` - Array of table names\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, list_tables, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"app.db\");\n\nlet tables = list_tables(db);\nfor (table in tables) {\n print(\"Table: \" + table);\n}\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### table_info(db, table_name)\n\nGets column information for a table.\n\n**Returns:** `array` - Array of column info objects\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, table_info, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"app.db\");\n\nlet columns = table_info(db, \"users\");\nfor (col in columns) {\n print(col.name + \" (\" + col.type + \")\");\n}\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Database Info\n\n### last_insert_id(db)\n\nGets the rowid of the last inserted row.\n\n**Returns:** `i64` - Last insert rowid\n\n### changes(db)\n\nGets the number of rows changed by the last statement.\n\n**Returns:** `i32` - Number of changes\n\n### total_changes(db)\n\nGets total changes since connection opened.\n\n**Returns:** `i32` - Total number of changes\n\n### db_error(db)\n\nGets the last error message.\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Error message\n\n### db_error_code(db)\n\nGets the last error code.\n\n**Returns:** `i32` - Error code\n\n### sqlite_version()\n\nGets the SQLite library version string.\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Version string (e.g., \"3.39.2\")\n\n### sqlite_version_number()\n\nGets the SQLite library version number.\n\n**Returns:** `i32` - Version number (e.g., 3039002)\n\n---\n\n## Data Types\n\nSQLite types are mapped to Hemlock types as follows:\n\n| SQLite Type | Hemlock Type |\n|-------------|--------------|\n| INTEGER | `i64` |\n| REAL | `f64` |\n| TEXT | `string` |\n| BLOB | `buffer` |\n| NULL | `null` |\n\nWhen binding parameters, Hemlock types are mapped as:\n\n| Hemlock Type | SQLite Type |\n|--------------|-------------|\n| `null` | NULL |\n| `bool` | INTEGER (0/1) |\n| `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `integer` | INTEGER |\n| `i64` | INTEGER (64-bit) |\n| `u8`, `u16`, `u32` | INTEGER |\n| `u64` | INTEGER (64-bit) |\n| `f32`, `f64`, `number` | REAL |\n| `string` | TEXT |\n| `buffer` | BLOB |\n\n---\n\n## Examples\n\n### CRUD Operations\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, exec, query, query_one, insert, update, delete_rows, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"todo.db\");\n\n// Create table\nexec(db, \"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS todos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, task TEXT, done INTEGER DEFAULT 0)\");\n\n// Create\nlet id = insert(db, \"INSERT INTO todos (task) VALUES (?)\", [\"Buy groceries\"]);\nprint(\"Created todo #\" + typeof(id));\n\n// Read all\nlet todos = query(db, \"SELECT * FROM todos\");\nfor (todo in todos) {\n let status = \"pending\";\n if (todo.done == 1) {\n status = \"done\";\n }\n print(\"[\" + status + \"] \" + todo.task);\n}\n\n// Read one\nlet todo = query_one(db, \"SELECT * FROM todos WHERE id = ?\", [id]);\nif (todo != null) {\n print(\"Found: \" + todo.task);\n}\n\n// Update\nlet changed = update(db, \"UPDATE todos SET done = 1 WHERE id = ?\", [id]);\nprint(\"Marked \" + typeof(changed) + \" todo(s) as done\");\n\n// Delete\nlet deleted = delete_rows(db, \"DELETE FROM todos WHERE done = 1\");\nprint(\"Deleted \" + typeof(deleted) + \" completed todo(s)\");\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### Batch Insert with Transaction\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, exec, begin, commit, prepare, stmt_exec, stmt_finalize, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\"data.db\");\nexec(db, \"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, message TEXT, level TEXT)\");\n\n// Batch insert with transaction for performance\nbegin(db);\n\nlet stmt = prepare(db, \"INSERT INTO logs (message, level) VALUES (?, ?)\");\n\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < 10000) {\n stmt_exec(stmt, [\"Log message \" + typeof(i), \"INFO\"]);\n i = i + 1;\n}\n\nstmt_finalize(stmt);\ncommit(db);\n\nprint(\"Inserted 10000 log entries\");\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### Join Queries\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, exec, query, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\":memory:\");\n\n// Create tables\nexec(db, \"CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)\");\nexec(db, \"CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER, total REAL)\");\n\n// Insert data\nexec(db, \"INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob')\");\nexec(db, \"INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 1, 99.99), (2, 1, 49.99), (3, 2, 149.99)\");\n\n// Join query\nlet results = query(db, \"\n SELECT u.name, SUM(o.total) as total_spent\n FROM users u\n JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id\n GROUP BY u.id\n ORDER BY total_spent DESC\n\");\n\nfor (row in results) {\n print(row.name + \" spent $\" + typeof(row.total_spent));\n}\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n### Using Blobs\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, exec, query, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\nlet db = open_db(\":memory:\");\nexec(db, \"CREATE TABLE files (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, data BLOB)\");\n\n// Create a buffer\nlet data = buffer(4);\ndata[0] = 0x89;\ndata[1] = 0x50;\ndata[2] = 0x4E;\ndata[3] = 0x47;\n\n// Insert blob\nexec(db, \"INSERT INTO files (name, data) VALUES (?, ?)\", [\"image.png\", data]);\n\n// Read blob\nlet rows = query(db, \"SELECT * FROM files WHERE name = ?\", [\"image.png\"]);\nif (rows.length > 0) {\n let file_data = rows[0].data;\n print(\"Retrieved \" + typeof(file_data.length) + \" bytes\");\n}\n\nclose_db(db);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling\n\nAll functions throw exceptions on errors:\n\n```hemlock\nimport { open_db, exec, close_db } from \"@stdlib/sqlite\";\n\ntry {\n let db = open_db(\"readonly.db\");\n\n try {\n exec(db, \"INVALID SQL SYNTAX\");\n } catch (e) {\n print(\"SQL Error: \" + e);\n }\n\n close_db(db);\n} catch (e) {\n print(\"Database Error: \" + e);\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Constants\n\n### Result Codes\n\n```hemlock\nSQLITE_OK // 0 - Success\nSQLITE_ERROR // 1 - Generic error\nSQLITE_BUSY // 5 - Database is busy\nSQLITE_LOCKED // 6 - Table is locked\nSQLITE_CONSTRAINT // 19 - Constraint violation\nSQLITE_MISMATCH // 20 - Data type mismatch\nSQLITE_ROW // 100 - sqlite3_step has another row\nSQLITE_DONE // 101 - sqlite3_step finished\n```\n\n### Column Types\n\n```hemlock\nSQLITE_INTEGER // 1\nSQLITE_FLOAT // 2\nSQLITE_TEXT // 3\nSQLITE_BLOB // 4\nSQLITE_NULL // 5\n```\n\n### Open Flags\n\n```hemlock\nSQLITE_OPEN_READONLY // Open read-only\nSQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE // Open read-write\nSQLITE_OPEN_CREATE // Create if not exists\n```\n\n---\n\n## Performance Tips\n\n1. **Use transactions for bulk operations** - Wrap multiple inserts/updates in `begin()`/`commit()`\n2. **Use prepared statements** - For repeated queries, prepare once and execute many times\n3. **Use parameter binding** - Never concatenate values into SQL strings\n4. **Close connections** - Always close databases when done\n5. **Use `:memory:`** - For temporary data, use in-memory databases\n\n---\n\n## Security Notes\n\n1. **Always use parameter binding** - Never build SQL with string concatenation\n2. **Validate table/column names** - Parameters can't be used for identifiers\n3. **Check return values** - Handle errors appropriately\n4. **Close connections** - Prevent resource leaks\n\n```hemlock\n// GOOD - Parameter binding\nexec(db, \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?\", [user_input]);\n\n// BAD - SQL injection vulnerability\nexec(db, \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '\" + user_input + \"'\");\n```\n\n---\n\n## System Requirements\n\n- SQLite3 shared library (`libsqlite3.so.0`)\n- On Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt-get install libsqlite3-dev`\n- On Fedora/RHEL: `sudo dnf install sqlite-devel`\n- On macOS: Usually pre-installed\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [SQLite Documentation](https://www.sqlite.org/docs.html)\n- `@stdlib/fs` - File system operations\n- `@stdlib/json` - JSON parsing for data export\n\n---\n\n## License\n\nPart of the Hemlock standard library.\n"}, "Biblioteca padrão -> strings": {"id": "stdlib-strings", "content": "# Hemlock Strings Module\n\nA standard library module providing advanced string utilities beyond the 18 built-in string methods.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe strings module provides utilities for:\n\n- **Padding & Alignment** - pad_left, pad_right, center\n- **Character Type Checking** - is_alpha, is_digit, is_alnum, is_whitespace\n- **String Manipulation** - reverse, lines, words\n- **Case Conversion** - snake_case, camel_case, pascal_case, kebab_case\n- **URL/Identifier** - slugify, truncate\n\nThese functions complement the built-in string methods (substr, slice, find, split, trim, to_upper, to_lower, etc.) with commonly-needed string operations.\n\n## Usage\n\n```hemlock\nimport { pad_left, pad_right, center } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\nimport { is_alpha, is_digit, is_alnum, is_whitespace } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\nimport { reverse, lines, words } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\nimport { snake_case, camel_case, pascal_case, kebab_case } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\nimport { slugify, truncate } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n```\n\nOr import all:\n\n```hemlock\nimport * as strings from \"@stdlib/strings\";\nlet result = strings.reverse(\"hello\");\n```\n\n---\n\n## Padding & Alignment\n\n### pad_left(str, width, fill?)\n\nPad string on the left to reach target width.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n- `width: i32` - Target width (in Unicode codepoints, not bytes)\n- `fill?: string` - Fill character (default: space `\" \"`)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Padded string\n\n**Notes:**\n- If string length >= width, returns original string unchanged\n- Fill must be exactly one character (one Unicode codepoint)\n- Padding length is calculated in codepoints (emoji = 1 character)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { pad_left } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nlet s1 = pad_left(\"42\", 5);\nprint(s1); // \" 42\"\n\nlet s2 = pad_left(\"42\", 5, \"0\");\nprint(s2); // \"00042\"\n\nlet s3 = pad_left(\"test\", 10, \"*\");\nprint(s3); // \"******test\"\n\n// Unicode fill character\nlet s4 = pad_left(\"Hi\", 5, \"🚀\");\nprint(s4); // \"🚀🚀🚀Hi\"\nprint(s4.length); // 5 (codepoints)\n```\n\n---\n\n### pad_right(str, width, fill?)\n\nPad string on the right to reach target width.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n- `width: i32` - Target width (in Unicode codepoints)\n- `fill?: string` - Fill character (default: space `\" \"`)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Padded string\n\n```hemlock\nimport { pad_right } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nlet s1 = pad_right(\"42\", 5);\nprint(s1); // \"42 \"\n\nlet s2 = pad_right(\"42\", 5, \"0\");\nprint(s2); // \"42000\"\n\n// Unicode fill\nlet s3 = pad_right(\"test\", 10, \"─\");\nprint(s3); // \"test──────\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### center(str, width, fill?)\n\nCenter string within target width.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n- `width: i32` - Target width (in Unicode codepoints)\n- `fill?: string` - Fill character (default: space `\" \"`)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Centered string\n\n**Notes:**\n- If total padding is odd, extra padding goes on the right\n- Useful for creating headers, banners, and aligned text\n\n```hemlock\nimport { center } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nlet s1 = center(\"Title\", 10);\nprint(s1); // \" Title \" (2 left, 3 right)\n\nlet s2 = center(\"X\", 5, \"*\");\nprint(s2); // \"**X**\"\n\n// Create banner\nlet banner = center(\"IMPORTANT\", 40, \"=\");\nprint(banner); // \"===============IMPORTANT================\"\n\n// Unicode fill\nlet s3 = center(\"test\", 10, \"─\");\nprint(s3); // \"───test───\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## Character Type Checking\n\nAll character type functions:\n- Return `false` for empty strings\n- Work with ASCII characters only (a-z, A-Z, 0-9)\n- Check **all** characters in the string (not just first)\n- Return `bool` result\n\n### is_alpha(str)\n\nCheck if string contains only alphabetic characters (a-z, A-Z).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - True if all characters are alphabetic\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_alpha } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(is_alpha(\"hello\")); // true\nprint(is_alpha(\"HELLO\")); // true\nprint(is_alpha(\"HelloWorld\")); // true\n\nprint(is_alpha(\"hello123\")); // false\nprint(is_alpha(\"hello world\")); // false (space)\nprint(is_alpha(\"hello!\")); // false\nprint(is_alpha(\"\")); // false (empty)\n```\n\n---\n\n### is_digit(str)\n\nCheck if string contains only digit characters (0-9).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - True if all characters are digits\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_digit } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(is_digit(\"123\")); // true\nprint(is_digit(\"0\")); // true\nprint(is_digit(\"999\")); // true\n\nprint(is_digit(\"123a\")); // false\nprint(is_digit(\"12.3\")); // false (decimal point)\nprint(is_digit(\"1 2 3\")); // false (spaces)\nprint(is_digit(\"\")); // false (empty)\n```\n\n---\n\n### is_alnum(str)\n\nCheck if string contains only alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - True if all characters are alphanumeric\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_alnum } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(is_alnum(\"hello123\")); // true\nprint(is_alnum(\"ABC123\")); // true\nprint(is_alnum(\"test\")); // true\nprint(is_alnum(\"123\")); // true\nprint(is_alnum(\"a1b2c3\")); // true\n\nprint(is_alnum(\"hello world\")); // false (space)\nprint(is_alnum(\"test!\")); // false (punctuation)\nprint(is_alnum(\"a-b\")); // false (hyphen)\nprint(is_alnum(\"\")); // false (empty)\n```\n\n**Common use case - validating identifiers:**\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_alnum } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nfn is_valid_identifier(name: string): bool {\n if (name.length == 0) {\n return false;\n }\n // First char must be alpha, rest can be alnum\n let first = name.slice(0, 1);\n if (!is_alpha(first)) {\n return false;\n }\n return is_alnum(name);\n}\n\nprint(is_valid_identifier(\"myVar123\")); // true\nprint(is_valid_identifier(\"123var\")); // false\n```\n\n---\n\n### is_whitespace(str)\n\nCheck if string contains only whitespace characters (space, tab, newline, carriage return).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - True if all characters are whitespace\n\n**Recognized whitespace:**\n- Space (U+0020)\n- Tab (U+0009)\n- Newline (U+000A)\n- Carriage return (U+000D)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_whitespace } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(is_whitespace(\" \")); // true\nprint(is_whitespace(\" \")); // true\nprint(is_whitespace(\"\\t\")); // true\nprint(is_whitespace(\"\\n\")); // true\nprint(is_whitespace(\"\\r\")); // true\nprint(is_whitespace(\" \\t\\n\")); // true\n\nprint(is_whitespace(\"hello\")); // false\nprint(is_whitespace(\" a \")); // false\nprint(is_whitespace(\"\")); // false (empty)\n```\n\n---\n\n## String Manipulation\n\n### reverse(str)\n\nReverse a string (works with Unicode codepoints).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Reversed string\n\n**Notes:**\n- Reverses by Unicode codepoints (not bytes)\n- Correctly handles emojis and multi-byte characters\n- O(n) time complexity where n = string length\n\n```hemlock\nimport { reverse } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(reverse(\"hello\")); // \"olleh\"\nprint(reverse(\"abc\")); // \"cba\"\nprint(reverse(\"12345\")); // \"54321\"\n\n// Single character\nprint(reverse(\"a\")); // \"a\"\n\n// Empty string\nprint(reverse(\"\")); // \"\"\n\n// Palindrome\nprint(reverse(\"racecar\")); // \"racecar\"\n\n// With spaces\nprint(reverse(\"hello world\")); // \"dlrow olleh\"\n\n// Unicode / emojis\nprint(reverse(\"🚀🌍\")); // \"🌍🚀\"\nprint(reverse(\"Hi🚀\")); // \"🚀iH\"\n```\n\n**Use case - palindrome checking:**\n\n```hemlock\nimport { reverse } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nfn is_palindrome(s: string): bool {\n let normalized = s.to_lower();\n return normalized == reverse(normalized);\n}\n\nprint(is_palindrome(\"racecar\")); // true\nprint(is_palindrome(\"Racecar\")); // true\nprint(is_palindrome(\"hello\")); // false\n```\n\n---\n\n### lines(str)\n\nSplit string into lines by newline characters.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n\n**Returns:** `array` - Array of strings (one per line)\n\n**Notes:**\n- Splits on `\\n` (newline) character\n- Empty lines are preserved as empty strings\n- Does not remove newlines from individual lines (they are split points)\n- Returns array with one element (the string itself) if no newlines\n\n```hemlock\nimport { lines } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\n// Basic line splitting\nlet l1 = lines(\"hello\\nworld\");\nprint(l1.length); // 2\nprint(l1[0]); // \"hello\"\nprint(l1[1]); // \"world\"\n\n// Multiple lines\nlet l2 = lines(\"line1\\nline2\\nline3\");\nprint(l2.length); // 3\n\n// Empty lines are preserved\nlet l3 = lines(\"a\\n\\nb\");\nprint(l3.length); // 3\nprint(l3[1]); // \"\" (empty line)\n\n// Single line (no newline)\nlet l4 = lines(\"hello\");\nprint(l4.length); // 1\nprint(l4[0]); // \"hello\"\n```\n\n**Use case - processing multi-line input:**\n\n```hemlock\nimport { lines } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nlet text = \"Alice\\nBob\\nCarol\\nDave\";\nlet names = lines(text);\n\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < names.length) {\n print(\"User \" + typeof(i + 1) + \": \" + names[i]);\n i = i + 1;\n}\n// Output:\n// User 1: Alice\n// User 2: Bob\n// User 3: Carol\n// User 4: Dave\n```\n\n---\n\n### words(str)\n\nSplit string into words by whitespace.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n\n**Returns:** `array` - Array of strings (non-empty words)\n\n**Notes:**\n- Splits on space character only (not tabs or newlines)\n- Filters out empty strings (multiple spaces create single split)\n- Trims each word (leading/trailing whitespace removed)\n- Returns empty array for empty string or whitespace-only string\n\n```hemlock\nimport { words } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\n// Basic word splitting\nlet w1 = words(\"hello world\");\nprint(w1.length); // 2\nprint(w1[0]); // \"hello\"\nprint(w1[1]); // \"world\"\n\n// Multiple words\nlet w2 = words(\"the quick brown fox\");\nprint(w2.length); // 4\n\n// Extra spaces (filtered out)\nlet w3 = words(\"hello world\");\nprint(w3.length); // 2 (not 3)\n\n// Leading/trailing spaces\nlet w4 = words(\" hello world \");\nprint(w4.length); // 2\n\n// Single word\nlet w5 = words(\"hello\");\nprint(w5.length); // 1\n\n// Empty string\nlet w6 = words(\"\");\nprint(w6.length); // 0\n\n// Only spaces\nlet w7 = words(\" \");\nprint(w7.length); // 0\n```\n\n**Use case - word counting:**\n\n```hemlock\nimport { words } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nfn word_count(text: string): i32 {\n return words(text).length;\n}\n\nlet text = \"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog\";\nprint(word_count(text)); // 9\n```\n\n---\n\n## Case Conversion\n\nThese functions convert between different casing conventions commonly used in programming.\n\n### snake_case(str)\n\nConvert string to snake_case (lowercase with underscores).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string (camelCase, PascalCase, kebab-case, or with spaces)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - snake_case string\n\n```hemlock\nimport { snake_case } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(snake_case(\"helloWorld\")); // \"hello_world\"\nprint(snake_case(\"HelloWorld\")); // \"hello_world\"\nprint(snake_case(\"hello-world\")); // \"hello_world\"\nprint(snake_case(\"Hello World\")); // \"hello_world\"\nprint(snake_case(\"XMLParser\")); // \"x_m_l_parser\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### camel_case(str)\n\nConvert string to camelCase (first word lowercase, subsequent words capitalized).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string (snake_case, kebab-case, or with spaces)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - camelCase string\n\n```hemlock\nimport { camel_case } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(camel_case(\"hello_world\")); // \"helloWorld\"\nprint(camel_case(\"hello-world\")); // \"helloWorld\"\nprint(camel_case(\"Hello World\")); // \"helloWorld\"\nprint(camel_case(\"HELLO_WORLD\")); // \"helloWorld\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### pascal_case(str)\n\nConvert string to PascalCase (UpperCamelCase - all words capitalized).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string (snake_case, kebab-case, or with spaces)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - PascalCase string\n\n```hemlock\nimport { pascal_case } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(pascal_case(\"hello_world\")); // \"HelloWorld\"\nprint(pascal_case(\"hello-world\")); // \"HelloWorld\"\nprint(pascal_case(\"hello world\")); // \"HelloWorld\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### kebab_case(str)\n\nConvert string to kebab-case (lowercase with hyphens).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string (camelCase, PascalCase, or with spaces/underscores)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - kebab-case string\n\n```hemlock\nimport { kebab_case } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(kebab_case(\"helloWorld\")); // \"hello-world\"\nprint(kebab_case(\"HelloWorld\")); // \"hello-world\"\nprint(kebab_case(\"hello_world\")); // \"hello-world\"\nprint(kebab_case(\"Hello World\")); // \"hello-world\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## URL/Identifier Utilities\n\n### slugify(str)\n\nConvert string to a URL-friendly slug.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n\n**Returns:** `string` - URL-safe slug (lowercase, hyphens, ASCII only)\n\n**Notes:**\n- Converts to lowercase\n- Replaces spaces, dashes, underscores with hyphens\n- Removes non-ASCII characters\n- Collapses multiple hyphens into one\n- Removes leading/trailing hyphens\n\n```hemlock\nimport { slugify } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(slugify(\"Hello World!\")); // \"hello-world\"\nprint(slugify(\" Foo Bar \")); // \"foo-bar\"\nprint(slugify(\"My Blog Post 2024\")); // \"my-blog-post-2024\"\nprint(slugify(\"Héllo Wörld\")); // \"hllo-wrld\" (non-ASCII removed)\nprint(slugify(\"@#$%Test!!!\")); // \"test\"\n```\n\n**Use case - URL generation:**\n\n```hemlock\nimport { slugify } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nfn article_url(title: string): string {\n return \"/blog/\" + slugify(title);\n}\n\nprint(article_url(\"My First Post!\")); // \"/blog/my-first-post\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### truncate(str, max_len, suffix?)\n\nTruncate string to maximum length with optional suffix.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `str` - Input string\n- `max_len: i32` - Maximum length (including suffix)\n- `suffix?: string` - Suffix to add if truncated (default: \"...\")\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Truncated string\n\n```hemlock\nimport { truncate } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(truncate(\"Hello World\", 8)); // \"Hello...\"\nprint(truncate(\"Hello\", 10)); // \"Hello\" (no truncation)\nprint(truncate(\"Hello World\", 8, \"..\")); // \"Hello..\"\nprint(truncate(\"Hello World\", 5, \"\")); // \"Hello\"\n```\n\n**Use case - display text:**\n\n```hemlock\nimport { truncate } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nfn display_title(title: string): string {\n return truncate(title, 30);\n}\n\nprint(display_title(\"A Very Long Article Title That Goes On\"));\n// \"A Very Long Article Title T...\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### from_bytes(src)\n\nBuild a string from raw bytes.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `src: buffer | array` - Byte source. A buffer's contents are copied\n as-is; an array's elements must be integers in 0-255.\n\n**Returns:** `string` - String containing exactly those bytes. No\ntranscoding is performed; rune-based operations (`.length`, `char_at`,\n`chars`) interpret the bytes as UTF-8.\n\n**Throws:** If `src` is not a buffer or array, or an array element is not\nan integer.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_bytes } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\nprint(from_bytes([72, 105, 33])); // \"Hi!\"\n\nlet buf = buffer(2);\nbuf[0] = 0xC3;\nbuf[1] = 0xA9;\nprint(from_bytes(buf)); // \"é\" (UTF-8 decoded)\nfree(buf);\n```\n\n**Use case - decoding network/binary payloads:**\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_bytes } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\n// Bytes accumulated from a socket or parsed out of a binary format\nfn payload_to_text(bytes: buffer): string {\n return from_bytes(bytes);\n}\n```\n\nThis is the documented replacement for the internal `__string_from_bytes`\nbuiltin. The inverse operation is the built-in `string.to_bytes()` method.\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling\n\nAll functions throw exceptions for invalid input:\n\n```hemlock\nimport { pad_left, is_alpha, reverse } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\n// Invalid fill character length\ntry {\n pad_left(\"test\", 10, \"ab\"); // Must be single character\n} catch (e) {\n print(\"Error: \" + e); // \"pad_left() fill must be single character\"\n}\n\n// Invalid type\ntry {\n is_alpha(123); // Must be string\n} catch (e) {\n print(\"Error: \" + e); // \"is_alpha() requires string argument\"\n}\n\n// Invalid type\ntry {\n reverse(null);\n} catch (e) {\n print(\"Error: \" + e); // \"reverse() requires string argument\"\n}\n```\n\n**Error messages:**\n- Clear indication of which function failed\n- Description of the problem (type mismatch, invalid length, etc.)\n- All errors are catchable with try/catch\n\n---\n\n## Performance Notes\n\n### Time Complexity\n\n- **pad_left, pad_right, center:** O(n) where n = padding length\n- **is_alpha, is_digit, is_alnum, is_whitespace:** O(n) where n = string length\n- **reverse:** O(n) where n = string length\n- **lines:** O(n) where n = string length\n- **words:** O(n) where n = string length\n\n### Memory Usage\n\n- **Padding functions:** Allocate new string with padding\n- **Character type functions:** Use `.chars()` which allocates array of runes\n- **reverse:** Allocates new string (does not modify in-place)\n- **lines, words:** Allocate new array of strings\n\n### Optimization Tips\n\n```hemlock\n// Bad - repeated checking in loop\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < items.length) {\n if (is_digit(items[i])) { // O(m) check per iteration\n // ...\n }\n i = i + 1;\n}\n\n// Better - check once, cache result if needed\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < items.length) {\n let item = items[i];\n let is_num = is_digit(item); // Cache result\n if (is_num) {\n // Use is_num multiple times\n }\n i = i + 1;\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Unicode Support\n\nAll functions are **Unicode-aware** and work with UTF-8 encoded strings:\n\n```hemlock\nimport { reverse, pad_left, pad_right, center } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\n// Reverse with emojis\nprint(reverse(\"Hello 🌍\")); // \"🌍 olleH\"\nprint(reverse(\"🚀🌟💫\")); // \"💫🌟🚀\"\n\n// Reverse with CJK characters\nprint(reverse(\"你好\")); // \"好你\"\nprint(reverse(\"こんにちは\")); // \"はちにんこ\"\n\n// Padding with Unicode\nlet s1 = pad_left(\"test\", 10, \"█\");\nprint(s1); // \"██████test\"\n\nlet s2 = pad_right(\"test\", 10, \"░\");\nprint(s2); // \"test░░░░░░\"\n\n// Centering with Unicode\nlet s3 = center(\"中\", 5, \"─\");\nprint(s3); // \"──中──\"\n```\n\n**Important notes:**\n- String length is measured in **Unicode codepoints** (not bytes)\n- Emoji count as 1 character: `\"🚀\".length == 1`\n- CJK characters count as 1 character each\n- Padding width is in codepoints\n\n---\n\n## Complete Example\n\n```hemlock\nimport { pad_left, pad_right, center } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\nimport { is_alpha, is_digit, is_alnum } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\nimport { reverse, lines, words } from \"@stdlib/strings\";\n\n// Create formatted table\nfn format_table(data: array): null {\n let header = center(\"USER DATA\", 40, \"=\");\n print(header);\n\n let i = 0;\n while (i < data.length) {\n let item = data[i];\n let id_str = pad_left(typeof(item.id), 5);\n let name_str = pad_right(item.name, 20);\n print(id_str + \" | \" + name_str);\n i = i + 1;\n }\n\n return null;\n}\n\n// Validate user input\nfn validate_username(name: string): bool {\n // Must be 3-20 characters, alphanumeric only\n if (name.length < 3 || name.length > 20) {\n return false;\n }\n return is_alnum(name);\n}\n\n// Parse multi-line config\nfn parse_config(text: string): array {\n let config_lines = lines(text);\n let result: array = [];\n\n let i = 0;\n while (i < config_lines.length) {\n let line = config_lines[i].trim();\n if (line.length > 0) {\n let parts = words(line);\n if (parts.length == 2) {\n result.push({ key: parts[0], value: parts[1] });\n }\n }\n i = i + 1;\n }\n\n return result;\n}\n\n// Example usage\nlet users = [\n { id: 1, name: \"Alice\" },\n { id: 42, name: \"Bob\" },\n { id: 999, name: \"Carol\" }\n];\n\nformat_table(users);\n\nprint(validate_username(\"alice123\")); // true\nprint(validate_username(\"ab\")); // false (too short)\nprint(validate_username(\"alice!\")); // false (not alnum)\n\nlet config_text = \"host localhost\\nport 8080\\nssl true\";\nlet config = parse_config(config_text);\nprint(config.length); // 3\n```\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n**Built-in string methods (18 total):**\n- Substring: `substr`, `slice`\n- Search: `find`, `contains`\n- Transform: `split`, `trim`, `to_upper`, `to_lower`, `replace`, `replace_all`, `repeat`\n- Prefix/suffix: `starts_with`, `ends_with`\n- Character access: `char_at`, `byte_at`, `chars`, `bytes`, `to_bytes`\n\n**Related stdlib modules:**\n- `@stdlib/decimal` - Number formatting, parsing, and StringBuilder\n- `@stdlib/regex` - Pattern matching with regular expressions\n- `@stdlib/json` - JSON parsing includes string escaping/unescaping\n- `@stdlib/collections` - Data structures for storing processed strings\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\nThe strings module has comprehensive test coverage:\n\n```bash\n# Run all strings tests\n./hemlock tests/stdlib_strings/test_padding.hml\n./hemlock tests/stdlib_strings/test_char_type.hml\n./hemlock tests/stdlib_strings/test_manipulation.hml\n./hemlock tests/stdlib_strings/test_errors.hml\n./hemlock tests/stdlib_strings/test_unicode.hml\n```\n\n**Test categories:**\n- Padding & alignment (45+ assertions)\n- Character type checking (35+ assertions)\n- String manipulation (40+ assertions)\n- Error handling (5+ assertions)\n- Unicode support (10+ assertions)\n\n---\n\n## Design Philosophy\n\nThe strings module follows Hemlock's design principles:\n\n1. **Explicit over implicit** - All functions have clear names and purposes\n2. **No magic** - Functions do exactly what their names suggest\n3. **Error transparency** - Exceptions for invalid input, not silent failures\n4. **Unicode-aware** - Full UTF-8 support for modern text processing\n5. **Complement built-ins** - Extends rather than duplicates built-in methods\n\n---\n\n## License\n\nPart of the Hemlock programming language standard library.\n"}, "Biblioteca padrão -> terminal": {"id": "stdlib-terminal", "content": "# Hemlock Terminal Module\n\nA standard library module providing ANSI terminal control for colors, cursor positioning, screen manipulation, and progress indicators.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe terminal module provides comprehensive terminal control:\n\n- **Colors** - 16 colors, bright variants, 256-color palette, RGB true color\n- **Styles** - Bold, italic, underline, dim, blink, reverse, hidden, strikethrough\n- **Cursor control** - Position, movement, save/restore, hide/show\n- **Screen control** - Clear screen/line, scroll\n- **Terminal info** - Get size, check color support\n- **Progress indicators** - Progress bars, spinners with multiple styles\n\n## Usage\n\n```hemlock\nimport { RED, GREEN, BOLD, clear, color } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\n// Colored text\nprint(RED + \"Error: Something went wrong\" + RESET);\nprint(color(\"Success!\", GREEN));\n\n// Styled text\nprint(BOLD + \"Important message\" + RESET);\n\n// Clear screen\nclear();\n```\n\nOr import all:\n\n```hemlock\nimport * as term from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\nprint(term.color(\"Hello\", term.BLUE));\n```\n\n---\n\n## Color Constants\n\n### Basic Colors (Foreground)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { BLACK, RED, GREEN, YELLOW, BLUE, MAGENTA, CYAN, WHITE } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(RED + \"Red text\" + RESET);\nprint(GREEN + \"Green text\" + RESET);\nprint(BLUE + \"Blue text\" + RESET);\n```\n\nAvailable colors:\n- `BLACK`, `RED`, `GREEN`, `YELLOW`, `BLUE`, `MAGENTA`, `CYAN`, `WHITE`\n\n### Bright Colors (Foreground)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { BRIGHT_RED, BRIGHT_GREEN, BRIGHT_BLUE, GRAY } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(BRIGHT_RED + \"Bright red\" + RESET);\nprint(GRAY + \"Gray text\" + RESET);\n```\n\nAvailable bright colors:\n- `GRAY`, `BRIGHT_RED`, `BRIGHT_GREEN`, `BRIGHT_YELLOW`, `BRIGHT_BLUE`, `BRIGHT_MAGENTA`, `BRIGHT_CYAN`, `BRIGHT_WHITE`\n\n### Background Colors\n\n```hemlock\nimport { BG_RED, BG_GREEN, BG_BLUE, WHITE } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(WHITE + BG_RED + \" Error \" + RESET);\nprint(WHITE + BG_GREEN + \" Success \" + RESET);\n```\n\nAvailable background colors:\n- `BG_BLACK`, `BG_RED`, `BG_GREEN`, `BG_YELLOW`, `BG_BLUE`, `BG_MAGENTA`, `BG_CYAN`, `BG_WHITE`\n- `BG_GRAY`, `BG_BRIGHT_RED`, `BG_BRIGHT_GREEN`, `BG_BRIGHT_YELLOW`, `BG_BRIGHT_BLUE`, `BG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA`, `BG_BRIGHT_CYAN`, `BG_BRIGHT_WHITE`\n\n---\n\n## Text Styles\n\n### Style Constants\n\n```hemlock\nimport { BOLD, ITALIC, UNDERLINE, DIM } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(BOLD + \"Bold text\" + RESET);\nprint(ITALIC + \"Italic text\" + RESET);\nprint(UNDERLINE + \"Underlined text\" + RESET);\nprint(DIM + \"Dim text\" + RESET);\n```\n\nAvailable styles:\n- `BOLD` - Bold/bright text\n- `DIM` - Dimmed text\n- `ITALIC` - Italic text (not supported on all terminals)\n- `UNDERLINE` - Underlined text\n- `BLINK` - Blinking text (rarely supported)\n- `REVERSE` - Reverse foreground/background\n- `HIDDEN` - Hidden text (still there, just invisible)\n- `STRIKETHROUGH` - Strikethrough text\n\n### Reset Styles\n\n```hemlock\nimport { BOLD, RESET_BOLD, UNDERLINE, RESET_UNDERLINE, RESET } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(BOLD + \"Bold \" + RESET_BOLD + \"not bold anymore\");\nprint(UNDERLINE + \"Underlined \" + RESET_UNDERLINE + \"not underlined\");\nprint(BOLD + UNDERLINE + \"Both \" + RESET + \"neither\");\n```\n\nReset specific styles:\n- `RESET` - Reset all styles and colors\n- `RESET_BOLD` - Reset bold only\n- `RESET_ITALIC` - Reset italic only\n- `RESET_UNDERLINE` - Reset underline only\n- `RESET_BLINK` - Reset blink only\n- `RESET_REVERSE` - Reset reverse only\n- `RESET_HIDDEN` - Reset hidden only\n\n### Combining Styles\n\n```hemlock\nimport { RED, BOLD, UNDERLINE, BG_YELLOW, RESET } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(BOLD + UNDERLINE + RED + \"Bold, underlined, red\" + RESET);\nprint(BOLD + RED + BG_YELLOW + \" Alert \" + RESET);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Color Functions\n\n### color(text, code)\nWrap text with a color code and automatically reset.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `text: string` - Text to colorize\n- `code: string` - Color code constant\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Colorized text with reset\n\n```hemlock\nimport { color, RED, GREEN, BLUE } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(color(\"Error\", RED));\nprint(color(\"Success\", GREEN));\nprint(color(\"Info\", BLUE));\n```\n\n### color_bg(text, fg, bg)\nWrap text with foreground and background colors.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `text: string` - Text to colorize\n- `fg: string` - Foreground color code\n- `bg: string` - Background color code\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Colorized text with reset\n\n```hemlock\nimport { color_bg, WHITE, RED, BG_RED, BG_GREEN } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(color_bg(\" ERROR \", WHITE, BG_RED));\nprint(color_bg(\" OK \", WHITE, BG_GREEN));\n```\n\n### rgb(r, g, b)\nCreate 24-bit RGB foreground color.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `r: i32` - Red component (0-255)\n- `g: i32` - Green component (0-255)\n- `b: i32` - Blue component (0-255)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - RGB color code\n\n```hemlock\nimport { rgb, RESET } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(rgb(255, 100, 50) + \"Custom orange\" + RESET);\nprint(rgb(75, 0, 130) + \"Indigo text\" + RESET);\n```\n\n**Note:** Requires terminal with true color support (24-bit color).\n\n### bg_rgb(r, g, b)\nCreate 24-bit RGB background color.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `r: i32` - Red component (0-255)\n- `g: i32` - Green component (0-255)\n- `b: i32` - Blue component (0-255)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - RGB background color code\n\n```hemlock\nimport { bg_rgb, rgb, RESET } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(rgb(255, 255, 255) + bg_rgb(255, 0, 0) + \" White on red \" + RESET);\n```\n\n### color_256(n)\nUse 256-color palette (foreground).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `n: i32` - Color index (0-255)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - 256-color code\n\n```hemlock\nimport { color_256, RESET } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\n// 0-15: Standard colors\n// 16-231: 6x6x6 color cube\n// 232-255: Grayscale\n\nprint(color_256(196) + \"Bright red\" + RESET);\nprint(color_256(21) + \"Deep blue\" + RESET);\n```\n\n**Color ranges:**\n- 0-15: Standard ANSI colors\n- 16-231: 6×6×6 RGB color cube\n- 232-255: Grayscale ramp\n\n### bg_color_256(n)\nUse 256-color palette (background).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `n: i32` - Color index (0-255)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - 256-color background code\n\n```hemlock\nimport { bg_color_256, color_256, RESET } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nprint(color_256(16) + bg_color_256(226) + \" Black on yellow \" + RESET);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Cursor Control\n\n### move_to(row, col)\nMove cursor to absolute position.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `row: i32` - Row (1-indexed, 1 = top)\n- `col: i32` - Column (1-indexed, 1 = left)\n\n**Returns:** `string` - ANSI escape sequence\n\n```hemlock\nimport { move_to } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nexec(\"printf '\" + move_to(10, 20) + \"Hello'\"); // Print at row 10, col 20\n```\n\n### move_up(n), move_down(n), move_left(n), move_right(n)\nMove cursor relative to current position.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `n: i32` - Number of positions to move\n\n**Returns:** `string` - ANSI escape sequence\n\n```hemlock\nimport { move_up, move_down, move_left, move_right } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\n// Move cursor up 3 lines\nexec(\"printf '\" + move_up(3) + \"'\");\n\n// Move cursor right 5 columns\nexec(\"printf '\" + move_right(5) + \"'\");\n```\n\n### Cursor Save/Restore\n\n```hemlock\nimport { SAVE_CURSOR, RESTORE_CURSOR } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\n// Save current position\nexec(\"printf '\" + SAVE_CURSOR + \"'\");\n\n// ... print something elsewhere ...\n\n// Restore saved position\nexec(\"printf '\" + RESTORE_CURSOR + \"'\");\n```\n\n**Constants:**\n- `SAVE_CURSOR` - Save cursor position (ANSI)\n- `RESTORE_CURSOR` - Restore cursor position (ANSI)\n- `SAVE_CURSOR_DEC` - Save cursor (DEC mode)\n- `RESTORE_CURSOR_DEC` - Restore cursor (DEC mode)\n\n### Cursor Visibility\n\n```hemlock\nimport { HIDE_CURSOR, SHOW_CURSOR } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\n// Hide cursor (useful for animations)\nexec(\"printf '\" + HIDE_CURSOR + \"'\");\n\n// ... do animation ...\n\n// Show cursor again\nexec(\"printf '\" + SHOW_CURSOR + \"'\");\n```\n\n**Note:** Always show cursor before exiting to avoid leaving terminal in bad state.\n\n---\n\n## Screen Control\n\n### Clear Screen\n\n```hemlock\nimport { CLEAR_SCREEN, CLEAR_TO_END, CLEAR_TO_START } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\n// Clear entire screen\nexec(\"printf '\" + CLEAR_SCREEN + \"'\");\n\n// Clear from cursor to end of screen\nexec(\"printf '\" + CLEAR_TO_END + \"'\");\n```\n\n**Constants:**\n- `CLEAR_SCREEN` - Clear entire screen\n- `CLEAR_TO_END` - Clear from cursor to end of screen\n- `CLEAR_TO_START` - Clear from cursor to start of screen\n\n### Clear Line\n\n```hemlock\nimport { CLEAR_LINE, CLEAR_LINE_TO_END } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\n// Clear entire line\nexec(\"printf '\\r\" + CLEAR_LINE + \"'\");\n\n// Clear from cursor to end of line\nexec(\"printf '\" + CLEAR_LINE_TO_END + \"'\");\n```\n\n**Constants:**\n- `CLEAR_LINE` - Clear entire line\n- `CLEAR_LINE_TO_END` - Clear from cursor to end of line\n- `CLEAR_LINE_TO_START` - Clear from cursor to start of line\n\n### Scrolling\n\n```hemlock\nimport { scroll_up, scroll_down } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\n// Scroll entire display up 3 lines\nexec(\"printf '\" + scroll_up(3) + \"'\");\n\n// Scroll entire display down 2 lines\nexec(\"printf '\" + scroll_down(2) + \"'\");\n```\n\n---\n\n## Terminal Info\n\n### size()\nGet terminal dimensions.\n\n**Parameters:** None\n\n**Returns:** `object` - `{ rows: i32, cols: i32 }`\n\n```hemlock\nimport { size } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nlet dimensions = size();\nprint(\"Terminal size: \" + typeof(dimensions.rows) + \"x\" + typeof(dimensions.cols));\n\n// Center text\nlet text = \"Hello, World!\";\nlet col = (dimensions.cols - text.length) / 2;\nprint_at(dimensions.rows / 2, col, text);\n```\n\n**Fallback:** Returns `{ rows: 24, cols: 80 }` if size cannot be determined.\n\n### supports_color()\nCheck if terminal supports ANSI colors.\n\n**Parameters:** None\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - True if colors are supported\n\n```hemlock\nimport { supports_color, RED, RESET } from \"@stdlib/terminal\";\n\nif (supports_color()) {\n print(RED + \"Colored output!\" + RESET);\n} else {\n print(\"No color support\");\n}\n```\n\n**Detection:** Checks `TERM` and `COLORTERM` environment variables.\n\n---\n\n## Progress Indicators\n\n### ProgressBar(total, width?)\nCreate a progress bar.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `total: i32` - Total number of items\n- `width: i32` (optional) - Bar width in characters (default: 40)\n\n**Returns:** Progress bar object\n\n**Methods:**\n- `update(value)` - Set progress to specific value\n- `increment()` - Increment progress by 1\n- `render()` - Manually render the bar\n-
